raw_segments.text: V. Nor would these be the only difficulties attendant upon the undertaking. If the Union
undertook to buy up the Negroes now in America, in order to transport them to Africa, the
price of slaves, increasing with their scarcity, would soon become enormous. And the States
of the North would never consent to expend such great sums for a purpose which would
procure such small advantages to themselves. If the Union took possession of the slaves
in the Southern States by force, or at a rate determined by law, an insurmountable resistance
would arise in that part of the country. Both alternatives are equally impossible.
